searches.note: Twenty two searches of twenty eight, six unspent. Three were restricted to a house's own domain (chambersrosewood.com.au, campbellswines.com.au, allsaintswine.com.au) and one to the Stanton and Killeen domains with Wine Companion, read as primary through their summaries; one to adb.anu.edu.au; the others blocked the house's domain so the second source would be independent. One search for the Chambers history returned nothing relevant. The classification search and the Tokay search serve every record. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: founding, people and dates, grapes, sites, making, ageing, serving, label words, every beat of the story, cards and questions; then the house rules.
Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source; where a detail stood in one source only it was cut or hedged as the house's account.
Writers' own sites met among the results (Wine with Seth, Tyson Stelzer, Chris Shanahan) are cited neither in the fragment nor here as a second source.

tested: The ladder and its ages (Rutherglen 3 to 5, Classic 6 to 10, Grand 11 to 19, Rare 20 and more): the producers' presentation, Explore Rutherglen and a Wine Australia bulletin. Sound; All Saints' fifteen year minimum is that house's own.

Founding of 1858, William Chambers from Norfolk, the rose hedge, the 1901 replanting, the grandson's soleras of the 1890s: the house's history (primary) and Liberty Wines, Wine Companion, Explore Rutherglen for 1858. Sound, the solera now hedged.
Phylloxera at Rutherglen in 1899: Harper's and the 1903 report of its spread at the Rutherglen college. Sound.

Bill Chambers: born 5 June 1933, died 14 December 2023, Roseworthy trained, a judge from 1964, back in Rutherglen in 1958 (The Rural) or 1956 (the house). Named with dates, the return given as the late 1950s.
Tokay: the agreement of 2008, in force from 2010, Tokay off Australian labels from 1 September 2020 (Wine Australia, Decanter, the Department of Agriculture). Changed.
Place: about a kilometre west of the township on the Corowa road (a merchant), the cellar door at Barkly Street. Sound.

swapNote: No swap proposed. The All Saints Rare and the Stanton and Killeen Vintage Fortified picks, which the author kept in doubt, are upheld: the Rare is the estate's wine at the top rung, the Museum filled to order; the house's own pages make vintage fortified the sixth generation's style.
questions: Ten questions read: each has one right answer, four options of a kind, the key never the longest by much, and an explanation naming the near miss. The Stanton and Killeen name question keys 1968, which the house's family history gives; see open.
codexTension: The library record of Chambers Rosewood calls Topaque a rename under the EU agreement, which stands; the region record's producers line for Chambers calls its Rare the benchmark of the top rung, a judging word in a published record, reported and not edited.
